question: What is the primary purpose of the cold chain in immunization?

options.A: To make sure syringes are sterile before an injection
options.B: To speed up the manufacturing process of new vaccines
options.C: To keep vaccines at the correct temperature until use
options.D: To freeze all vaccines solid for long-term transport

explanation: The cold chain ensures vaccines stay within safe temperature limits from the factory to the patient. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h1)

question: What happens to a vaccine when the cold chain is broken?

options.A: It becomes stronger and requires a smaller dose
options.B: It changes color but remains completely safe to use
options.C: It loses its potency and fails to protect the patient
options.D: It turns into a dangerous liquid poison immediately

explanation: Temperature exposures outside the recommended range permanently destroy the active components of the vaccine. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h1)

question: Why are domestic food refrigerators discouraged for storing vaccines?

options.A: They lack doors that can be locked with a padlock
options.B: They are too small to hold more than two vials
options.C: They consume too much electricity for a clinic budget
options.D: They experience wide and unsafe temperature fluctuations

explanation: Food refrigerators are not built to hold steady temperatures within the narrow range required for vaccines. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of conditioning an ice pack before putting it in a vaccine carrier?

options.A: To prevent freezing and damaging sensitive vaccines
options.B: To melt the ice completely into warm water first
options.C: To make the ice pack lighter for the community health worker
options.D: To freeze the vaccines faster during transport

explanation: Conditioned ice packs have warmed up slightly so they do not cause accidental freezing of liquid vaccines inside the carrier. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h2)

question: What is a major risk of allowing thick frost to build up inside a vaccine refrigerator?

options.A: It turns all the liquid vaccines into solid blocks
options.B: It causes the outside walls to become very hot
options.C: It reduces the cooling efficiency of the appliance
options.D: It creates an unpleasant smell inside the storage unit

explanation: Excess frost acts as an insulation layer that prevents the refrigerator from maintaining its proper internal temperature. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h3)

question: A nurse notices that the cleaning staff plugged an electric kettle into the same socket used for the vaccine refrigerator. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Leave both plugged in as long as the electricity is stable
options.B: Unplug the kettle and ensure the refrigerator has a dedicated socket
options.C: Move the kettle to another room only when patients are present
options.D: Switch off the refrigerator while the kettle is boiling water

explanation: Vaccine refrigerators must always have a dedicated power source to prevent accidental tripping or power overloads. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h3)

question: What is the safe temperature range for storing most routine vaccines in a refrigerator?
explanation: Most standard vaccines must be kept refrigerated within the +2°C to +8°C range to maintain their potency. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h4)

question: Why must clinic staff record refrigerator temperatures at least twice every single day?

options.A: To calculate the exact electricity bill for the vaccine unit
options.B: To catch and correct temperature excursions before vaccines spoil
options.C: To make sure the electric fan spins at maximum speed
options.D: To fulfill government paperwork requirements with no real benefit

explanation: Routine checks allow nurses to spot equipment failures early and move vaccines to safety before they are ruined. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h4)

question: Which cleaning practice is correct for reusable vaccine carriers and plastic trays?

options.A: Scrubbing with harsh steel wool and bleach solution
options.B: Washing with mild soap and water, then air-drying
options.C: Wiping them with dirty rags used for the clinic floor
options.D: Submerging them in boiling oil to remove all dirt

explanation: Mild soap and water clean the equipment safely without leaving harmful chemical residues that could affect vaccines. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h5)

question: What is the danger of using harsh chemical disinfectants on vaccine storage containers without proper rinsing?

options.A: The cold chain temperature will drop below freezing
options.B: Chemical residues can contaminate and damage the vaccines
options.C: The plastic container will instantly melt into a liquid
options.D: The container will attract more dust from the clinic air

explanation: Leftover chemical residues can interact with vials or equipment, compromising safety and sterility. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h5)

question: The vaccine refrigerator temperature is rising and the motor is completely silent. What is the very first thing the nurse should check?

options.A: The manufacturer phone number in another city
options.B: The expiration date of every single vial inside
options.C: The amount of frost built up on the freezer walls
options.D: The electrical plug and wall socket connection

explanation: Checking the power source is the fastest and most common first step when an appliance stops running altogether. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h6)

question: What should a nurse do first if a refrigerator fails completely during a long power outage?

options.A: Transfer the vaccines into a cold box with conditioned ice packs
options.B: Throw away all vaccines immediately without checking them
options.C: Wait patiently until the electricity returns on its own
options.D: Leave the refrigerator door wide open to let fresh air inside

explanation: Moving vaccines to a pre-packed cold box preserves the cold chain while alternative power or repair is arranged. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h6)

question: What is the main reason healthcare workers should NOT recap needles after giving an injection?

options.A: It is the leading cause of accidental needle-stick injuries
options.B: It wastes valuable clinic time during busy immunizations
options.C: It makes the safety box fill up much faster than normal
options.D: It breaks the plunger inside the plastic syringe barrel

explanation: Trying to recap needles often leads to accidental punctures to the fingers and hands of the nurse. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h7)

question: When should a puncture-resistant safety box for used syringes be sealed and prepared for disposal?

options.A: When it is filled up to the three-quarters mark
options.B: At the end of every working hour regardless of volume
options.C: When every single inch to the absolute brim is packed
options.D: Only when an external supervisor visits the clinic

explanation: Stopping at three-quarters prevents overfilling and lowers the risk of accidental punctures from protruding needles. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h7)

question: What does the FEFO inventory rule stand for in vaccine management?
explanation: FEFO ensures that vaccines nearing their expiration date are used before newer supplies to prevent wastage. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h8)

question: Why is keeping a detailed maintenance log for cold chain equipment important?

options.A: It allows staff to test the freezing point of water ice
options.B: It reduces the amount of electricity the refrigerator uses
options.C: It helps plan for timely repairs and equipment replacements
options.D: It replaces the need to check temperatures twice daily

explanation: Maintenance logs track the performance history of appliances, making it easier to justify buying replacements before breakdowns occur. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h8)
